moments.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

points: Josiah had four sons: Johanan, Jehoiakim, Zedekiah and Shallum; Jehoiakim's son Jeconiah is the Jehoiachin of Kings and the Jechonias of Matthew.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

points: The sons of Jeconiah were Assir and Salathiel, and Salathiel's brothers included Pedaiah; whether Assir is a name or a title for the captive makes no difference to the line.
Pedaiah had a son named Zerubbabel; so Salathiel's nephew was also a Zerubbabel, and the name means born in Babylon, a common name for children born in that captivity.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

points: The sons born to David in Hebron are named, from Amnon the firstborn to the sixth, with their mothers.
Amnon was the son who defiled his sister Tamar, and Absalom, named here among the younger sons, later avenged her and paid for it with his own life.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 3: The Sons of David and the Kings of Judah

points: David reigned in Hebron seven years and six months before he reigned in Jerusalem.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 3: The Sons of David and the Kings of Judah

points: The sons born to David in Jerusalem are named, including Solomon, born of Bathshua the daughter of Ammiel.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 3: The Sons of David and the Kings of Judah

points: Nine sons are set down here besides the sons of the concubines, and their sister Tamar is named among them.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 3: The Sons of David and the Kings of Judah

points: The kings of Judah are set down in order from Solomon: Rehoboam, Abijah, Asa, Jehoshaphat, and on through the line.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 3: The Sons of David and the Kings of Judah

points: The record runs through Hezekiah, Manasseh, Amon, and Josiah, keeping the royal succession by name.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 3: The Sons of David and the Kings of Judah

points: The sons of Jeconiah are named, and the line is carried through Salathiel, Pedaiah, and Zerubbabel after the captivity.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 3: The Sons of David and the Kings of Judah

points: The record runs on through the sons of Zerubbabel and their descendants, and these too are our forefathers, kept by name so we can search out our fathers.
